title: How can one power be split in three different ways?
description: Three numbers are each written as a multiplication of powers in three different ways, using the exponent rules from the worked example. The trick is to make one base and then split the exponent in different ways. A number check on part one closes the working.
teaching_notes: One idea: write the number with a common base, then split its exponent into parts that add up to the same total. Watch for students who split an exponent into parts that do not add up, or who forget that a base like four needs its exponent changed.

video_script.why: A learner uses the rule for adding exponents in reverse, to split one power into a multiplication of powers in different ways.
video_script.substitution: the book's own three numbers: sixty four cubed, one hundred and ninety two to the power eight and thirty two to the power negative five
video_script.anchor: the three numbers 64^3, 192^8 and 32^-5 written in a column on the board
video_script.payoff_line: Each way is a different split of the same exponent

final_answer.value: For example (i) 2 to the power 10 × 2 to the power 8, 4 to the power 5 × 4⁴, 8³ × 8³ (ii) 2 to the power 48 × 3 to the power 8, 64 to the power 8 × 3 to the power 8, 12 to the power 8 × 16 to the power 8 (iii) 2 to the power −10 × 2 to the power −15, 4 to the power −5 × 8 to the power −5, 2 to the power 5 × 2 to the power −30
final_answer.spoken: for example, part one: two to the power ten times two to the power eight, four to the power five times four to the power four, and eight cubed times eight cubed; part two: two to the power forty eight times three to the power eight, sixty four to the power eight times three to the power eight, and twelve to the power eight times sixteen to the power eight; part three: two to the power negative ten times two to the power negative fifteen, four to the power negative five times eight to the power negative five, and two to the power five times two to the power negative thirty

video_script.design: One idea: one common base, then split the exponent. Each part gets its own step with the three ways side by side; the last split of part one is held back for the answer, and a number check closes the working.

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This question is from your book.
<bookmark mark='write'/>Write each number as a multiplication of two or more powers, in three different ways.
<bookmark mark='one'/>Part one is sixty four cubed.
<bookmark mark='two'/>Part two is one hundred and ninety two to the power eight.
<bookmark mark='three'/>Part three is thirty two to the power negative five.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Can you find three ways?

beats.on_screen: 2^5 = 2^2 x 2^3 because 2 + 3 = 5: one exponent split into two parts

marks.same: the worked example from the book is set beside the three numbers

narration: <bookmark mark='same'/>We solve this the same way as the example in your book.
<bookmark mark='split'/>There we added exponents. Here we split an exponent into parts.
<bookmark mark='ex'/>Two to the power five is two squared times two cubed, because two plus three is five.

marks.given: the three numbers are written in a column

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, three numbers, and each one is a power.

beats.on_screen: To find: three ways for each, as a multiplication of powers

marks.find: the words three ways for each, as a multiplication of powers are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to write each number in three ways, as a multiplication of powers.
<bookmark mark='base'/>Step one, make the base two. Sixty four is two to the power six.
<bookmark mark='exp'/>Six times three is eighteen, so the number is two to the power eighteen.
<bookmark mark='w1'/>Break eighteen into ten plus eight.
<bookmark mark='w2'/>Four to the power nine works too, with nine as five plus four.
<bookmark mark='w3'/>Eight to the power six works too, with six as three plus three.
<bookmark mark='split'/>Step two, one hundred and ninety two is sixty four times three. That is two to the power six times three.
<bookmark mark='eight'/>Each factor gets the power eight. That gives two to the power forty eight times three to the power eight.
<bookmark mark='w2'/>Two to the power six is sixty four. Keeping it gives sixty four to the power eight times three to the power eight.
<bookmark mark='w3'/>Also, one hundred and ninety two is twelve times sixteen. That gives twelve to the power eight times sixteen to the power eight.
<bookmark mark='base'/>Step three, thirty two is two to the power five.
<bookmark mark='exp'/>Five times negative five is negative twenty five.
<bookmark mark='w1'/>Break negative twenty five into negative ten plus negative fifteen.
<bookmark mark='w2'/>Four times eight is thirty two. That gives four to the power negative five times eight to the power negative five.
<bookmark mark='w3'/>Or break negative twenty five into five plus negative thirty.

marks.same: 1024 x 256 = 262144 is written and joined to 64^3 = 262144

narration: <bookmark mark='chk'/>Step four, check part one with numbers. Two to the power ten is one thousand and twenty four.
<bookmark mark='eight'/>Two to the power eight is two hundred and fifty six.
<bookmark mark='same'/>Their multiplication is two lakh sixty two thousand one hundred and forty four. Sixty four cubed is the same.
